To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

deep learning methods can significantly improve the performance of online motor imagery based BCSs and that the benefits of deep learning methods are most pronounced in participants who have the most difficulty controlling the system.
deep learning classification improves offline BCI accuracy and increases online BCI performance.

deep learning methods increase offline classification accuracy of a longitudinal online motor imagery based BCl dataset, and significantly increase information transfer rates of a BCI system without loss of classification accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of deep neural networks to the classification of continuous, online EEG data from a BCI system, with the goal of increasing the performance of the BCI.
the application of deep neural networks to noninvasive motor imagery BCI and the benefits that this approach may offer.
the application of deep neural networks to the analysis of continuous noninvasive BCLs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the benefits of deep learning classification of continuous noninvasive brain computer interface control is that it increases the classification accuracy and information transfer rate of a BCI system.
deep learning methods improve the performance of non-invasive BCI in practical scenarios.

deep learning methods improve the classification accuracy of noninvasive motor imagery BCIs, and these improvements are especially valuable to those who need them most, and that deep learning methods can extract valuable information from outside the motor cortex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep learning methods can be used to improve the performance of BCI in a practical, continuous control task, even in cases where the BCI users are not highly proficient.
deep learning methods can be used to improve BCI performance, especially for participants who have the most difficulty using BCI.

deep learning methods can significantly improve BCI classification accuracy in a continuous control task and that these improvements are most pronounced for users with low initial online BCI accuracy and when using full scalp electrode montages.
The main takeaway from our work is that
deep learning methods can be successfully applied to continuous BCI control tasks, and that these methods can improve BCI performance for a variety of users.
deep learning based methods can be used to increase the information transfer rate of a BCI, even in a longitudinal setting with multiple classes and continuous feedback.
deep learning methods can significantly improve noninvasive BCL performance and may be especially beneficial for users with lower initial performance.
